headline: South Asia: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims.
- Asia: Could Beijing’s HQ-17 air-defence system defend PLA amphibious forces from Taiwan strikes?.
- Western Russia: Romanian PM condemns Russian attack on three commercial vessels in Black Sea.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: We’ve broken the glass ceiling, but have we overcome? – Luz Longsworth.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: We’ve broken the glass ceiling, but have we overcome? – Luz Longsworth.
WESTERN BUREAU: Women have shattered glass ceilings, claimed executive offices, and risen to the highest levels of leadership. But Dr Luz Longsworth is challenging the notion that reaching the top means the battle is won. “We have broken a lot of ceilings, but we have not overcome,” the veteran academic and corporate leader declared last Wednesday evening, warning that women’s growing presence in powerful positions should not be mistaken for the disappearance of barriers to their success. “Don’t let our firsts be our lasts,” she urged.

Odesa authorities have confirmed that civilian infrastructure across the region – including grain warehouses and a car dealership in Odesa – was destroyed in fires caused by a Russian attack on 15 November.

Ukraine's General Staff says a strike on Russia's Akhtubinsk airfield caused a secondary detonation at a missile kit depot, and a drone launch site in Oryol Oblast was hit.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir have shared the top spot in the latest edition of the world’s 500 most influential Muslims, alongside the Saudi king and crown prince and the Turkish president. The rankings have been compiled by the Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre (RISSC), a research institute based in Amman, Jordan. It has been publishing an annual report titled “The 500 Most Influential Muslims” since 2009, recognising and highlighting individuals who have made significant contributions to Muslim communities.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: Blasts rattle Bahrain as Iran launches second drone attack in 3 days.
Blasts echoed over Bahrain on Sunday as the tiny Gulf nation was rattled by the second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East war. Sirens rang out, and authorities posted several alerts on social media urging residents to seek shelter, their first warnings since September. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they carried out a drone attack on a US radar system in the desert island state, which hosts US military facilities including a major naval base.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: Authorities ban gatherings in five districts of KP for 30 days, citing law and order situation.
BANNU/BAJAUR/LAKKI MARWAT/SWABI: The district administrations of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bannu, Bajaur, Lakki Marwat, Swabi and Tank on Sunday imposed Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) for a month, banning public gatherings and several other activities amid the prevailing law and order situation. Three of the five districts — Bannu, Bajaur and Tank — are among the 12 districts that were deemed to face intense security challenges and special emergency measures were imposed there.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 17 hours ago: Middle power aspirations.
AS the global order shifts away from unipolarity toward fragmented multipolarity, middle powers have gained unprecedented strategic weight. In a fragmented multipolar world, middle powers serve as indispensable diplomatic bridges and economic shock absorbers that keep the international system functioning despite great-power paralysis. Middle powers lack hegemonic ambitions, and retain the credibility to mediate active conflicts, build agile issue-specific coalitions, and maintain open trade and supply-chain corridors across rival blocs.

Samir Abu Younis, 53, the commander of the Rafah brigade, was killed on Saturday, said the Palestinian militant group’s armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades. A Jordanian court on Sunday sentenced three men to death by hanging over a deadly church shooting, as the kingdom’s Christmas celebrations were cancelled in solidarity with the victims’ families. Gunmen killed nine people and wounded 25 others when they stormed a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in southern Hammoud village, Karak governorate, on October 23. New state media footage has surfaced showing for the first time what appears to be a Chinese-modified variant of the Russian-origin Kh-29T air-to-surface missile mounted on a J-10C fighter jet. State broadcaster CCTV’s social media account posted a video on Wednesday featuring Chinese fighters, showing the missile mounted under the 4.5-generation fighter as it took off, according to posts by Chinese military bloggers over the weekend. - Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Cong suggests Army ‘friendly fire’ behind deaths of 2 SPOs in Kishtwar, BJP hits back.
In Jammu and Kashmir, Congress has called for a thorough investigation into the tragic killing of two special police officers. Initial reports indicate that the officers may have been accidentally shot by Army personnel during a hunting operation. The BJP has dismissed these allegations, claiming they tarnish the integrity of the security forces.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Massive Anti-Terrorist Operation Launched In Kashmir Over Kulgam Attack.
The Jammu and Kashmir police, the Army and the CRPF have jointly launched the operation. Top police officers, including J&K DGP Nalin Parvati and the Inspector General of Kashmir Zone, Sujit Kumar, are personally supervising the operation.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Morning Mail: gender-diverse Australians barred from US subs; Victoria’s election explained; and World Cup triumph.
- The Guardian - Australia, 2 hours ago: Morning Mail: gender-diverse Australians barred from US subs; Victoria’s election explained; and World Cup triumph.
Want to get this in your inbox every weekday? Sign up for the Morning Mail here, and finish your day with our Politics, really newsletter. Good morning. Documents have revealed how gender diverse sailors are explicitly banned from Australia’s nuclear submarine training program because of US military policies prohibiting transgender service personnel. Meanwhile, we head to a tiny atoll in Papua New Guinea’s sprawling archipelago where the climate crisis is biting hard – and a “supercharged” El Niño has brought searing heat, brutal drought, and water shortages.
- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: Vanuatu woman internationally recognised for solar scheme tackling violence.
Women in a village on Vanuatu's Tanna island are working to reduce their risk of being attacked by switching from candles to solar lights.
- The Guardian - Australia, 7 hours ago: Gender-diverse Australian sailors barred from US submarines despite Aukus deal, documents reveal.
Defence briefing released under freedom of information laws shows ADF beholden to US directives when in training Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Aukus is effectively forcing the Australian navy to comply with a US ban on transgender people in the military with gender-diverse navy recruits prevented from starting a career in nuclear submarines because they would not be safe training on US boats.
- The Guardian - Australia, just now: How sensitive data from Centrelink and other Australian agencies may have been fed to Palantir software.
Exclusive: Personal information of Centrelink clients and childcare workers is among data shared with ACIC, which uses US tech company’s software The personal information of Centrelink customers, taxpayers and childcare workers is among a trove of sensitive data that may be ending up in Palantir’s surveillance software in Australia, without the departments responsible for the information even knowing about it.
